import re, os, subprocess, sys, json

ROOT = "/mnt/raid/home/yangshuangning/vuln_variant_search/experiments/clairvoyant_variant_search/runs/10_cluster/C7/public/snapshots/s03"

# Step 1: find all NAPI poll function names wired via netif_napi_add(...)
napi_polls = {}   # pollfn -> list of (file, line)
napi_calls = []   # (file, line, pollfn)
out = subprocess.run(["/usr/bin/rg", "-n", "--no-heading", "-g", "*.c",
                      r"netif_napi_add", "drivers", "net"],
                     cwd=ROOT, capture_output=True, text=True).stdout
for line in out.splitlines():
    m = re.match(r"([^:]+):(\d+):(.*)", line)
    if not m: continue
    f, ln, txt = m.group(1), int(m.group(2)), m.group(3)
    # netif_napi_add(dev, &napi, poll_fn, weight)
    mm = re.search(r"netif_napi_add(?:_exclusive|_weight|_irq)?\s*\(([^;]*)", txt)
    if not mm: continue
    args = mm.group(1)
    parts = [p.strip() for p in args.split(",")]
    # poll fn is typically 3rd arg
    fn = None
    for p in parts[1:4]:
        if re.match(r"^[a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*$", p) and p not in ("NAPI_POLL_WEIGHT",):
            if parts.index(p) >= 1:
                fn = p; break
    if fn:
        napi_polls.setdefault(fn, []).append((f, ln))
        napi_calls.append((f, ln, fn))

print(f"NAPI poll fns found: {len(napi_polls)}")

# Step 2: find tasklet callbacks wired via tasklet_init/tasklet_setup/DECLARE_TASKLET
tasklet_cbs = {}
out2 = subprocess.run(["/usr/bin/rg", "-n", "--no-heading", "-g", "*.c",
                       r"tasklet_init\s*\(|tasklet_setup\s*\(|DECLARE_TASKLET", "drivers", "net"],
                      cwd=ROOT, capture_output=True, text=True).stdout
for line in out2.splitlines():
    m = re.match(r"([^:]+):(\d+):(.*)", line)
    if not m: continue
    f, ln, txt = m.group(1), int(m.group(2)), m.group(3)
    mm = re.search(r"tasklet_(?:init|setup)\s*\([^,]+,\s*([a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*)", txt)
    if mm:
        tasklet_cbs.setdefault(mm.group(1), []).append((f, ln))
        continue
    mm = re.search(r"DECLARE_TASKLET(?:_DISABLED)?\s*\(\s*([a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*)\s*,\s*([a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*)", txt)
    if mm:
        tasklet_cbs.setdefault(mm.group(2), []).append((f, ln))

print(f"tasklet cbs found: {len(tasklet_cbs)}")

# Step 3: extract function bodies for all these callbacks, look for plain spin_lock
def extract_body(fname, fn):
    path = os.path.join(ROOT, fname)
    try:
        src = open(path, errors="replace").read()
    except OSError:
        return None, None
    # find definition: fn(...) {  ... may be multi-line signature
    pat = re.compile(r"^[ \t]*(?:static\s+)?(?:inline\s+)?(?:void|int|irqreturn_t|u\d+|unsigned|long|bool)\s+" + re.escape(fn) + r"\s*\(", re.M)
    m = pat.search(src)
    if not m:
        pat2 = re.compile(r"^[ \t]*" + re.escape(fn) + r"\s*\(", re.M)
        m = pat2.search(src)
        if not m:
            return None, None
    start = m.start()
    # find opening brace after signature
    bidx = src.find("{", m.end())
    if bidx == -1: return None, None
    depth = 0
    i = bidx
    while i < len(src):
        c = src[i]
        if c == "{": depth += 1
        elif c == "}":
            depth -= 1
            if depth == 0: break
        i += 1
    body = src[bidx:i+1]
    line_no = src[:start].count("\n") + 1
    return body, line_no

results = []
for kind, cmap in (("napi", napi_polls), ("tasklet", tasklet_cbs)):
    for fn, sites in cmap.items():
        for (f, ln) in sites:
            body, defline = extract_body(f, fn)
            if body is None: continue
            if "spin_lock" not in body: continue
            # find plain spin_lock( (not _bh, _irq, _irqsave, _nested...)
            plain = re.findall(r"spin_lock(?:_nested(?:_irqsave)?)?\s*\(\s*([^;]+?)\s*\)", body)
            plain = [p for p in plain if "flags" not in p.split(",")[-1:][0][:40] or True]
            bh = re.findall(r"spin_lock_bh\s*\(", body)
            irq = re.findall(r"spin_lock_irq(?:save)?\s*\(", body)
            if plain:
                results.append({
                    "kind": kind, "fn": fn, "file": f, "reg_line": ln, "def_line": defline,
                    "plain_locks": plain, "bh_sites": len(bh), "irq_sites": len(irq),
                })

print(f"callbacks with plain spin_lock in body: {len(results)}")
for r in results:
    print(f"[{r['kind']}] {r['fn']}  {r['file']}:{r['def_line']} (reg@{r['reg_line']}) plain={r['plain_locks']} bh={r['bh_sites']} irq={r['irq_sites']}")

with open(os.path.join(os.environ.get("TMPDIR","/tmp"), "i032", "scan_results.json"), "w") as fh:
    json.dump(results, fh, indent=2)
EOF

import re, os, sys, subprocess, json, glob

ROOT="/mnt/radium"  # placeholder
ROOT="/mnt/raid/home/yangshuangning/vuln_variant_search/experiments/clairvoyant_variant_search/runs/10_cluster/C7/public/snapshots/s03"
DIRS=["drivers/net","drivers/staging","net","drivers/atm","drivers/isdn","drivers/usb/gadget","drivers/tty","drivers/char","drivers/scsi","drivers/mmc","drivers/iio"]
files=[]
for d in DIRS:
    out=subprocess.run(["find",os.path.join(ROOT,d),"-name","*.c"],capture_output=True,text=True)
    files+= [f for f in out.stdout.split() ]
files=sorted(set(files))
print("files:",len(files),file=sys.stderr)

def read(p):
    try:
        return open(p,encoding="utf-8",errors="replace").read()
    except: return ""

# regex for function definitions at col 0: type name(args)\n{
FUNC_RE=re.compile(r'^[A-Za-z_][\w\s\*,\(\)\[\]\.]*?\b([A-Za-z_]\w*)\s*\([^;{}]*\)\s*\{', re.M)

def extract_funcs(src):
    funcs={}  # name -> (startline, body)
    for m in FUNC_RE.finditer(src):
        name=m.group(1)
        bstart=m.end()-1  # position of '{'
        depth=0; i=bstart
        while i < len(src):
            c=src[i]
            if c=='{': depth+=1
            elif c=='}':
                depth-=1
                if depth==0: break
            i+=1
        body=src[bstart:i+1]
        line=src[:m.start()].count('\n')+1
        # avoid redef better: keep first or longest
        if name not in funcs or len(body)>len(funcs[name][1]):
            funcs[name]=(line,body)
    return funcs

CALL_RE=re.compile(r'\b([A-Za-z_]\w*)\s*\(')

results=[]
for f in files:
    src=read(f)
    if not src: continue
    if 'tasklet' not in src and 'napi' not in src: continue
    # softirq entries
    soft=set()
    for m in re.finditer(r'tasklet_init\s*\(\s*[^,]+,\s*([A-Za-z_]\w*)\s*,',src):
        soft.add(m.group(1))
    for m in re.finditer(r'DECLARE_TASKLET(?:_OLD)?\s*\(\s*\w+\s*,\s*([A-Za-z_]\w*)',src):
        soft.add(m.group(1))
    for m in re.finditer(r'tasklet_(?:hi_)?schedule\s*\(',src):
        pass
    for m in re.finditer(r'netif_napi_add\s*\([^;]*?,\s*([A-Za-z_]\w*)\s*,',src):
        soft.add(m.group(1))
    # napi poll assigned via struct? also &dev->napi etc handled by name
    if not soft: continue
    funcs=extract_funcs(src)
    # build intra-file call graph
    def calls(body):
        return set(CALL_RE.findall(body))
    graph={n:calls(b) & set(funcs) for n,(l,b) in funcs.items()}
    # reachability from soft entries
    reach=set()
    stack=[s for s in soft if s in funcs]
    while stack:
        n=stack.pop()
        if n in reach: continue
        reach.add(n)
        stack.extend(graph.get(n,()))
    # find plain spin_lock sites in reachable funcs
    for n in reach:
        line0,body=funcs[n]
        for m in re.finditer(r'spin_lock(?:_nested)?\(\s*([^)]+)\)',body):
            lock=m.group(1).strip()
            bl=line0+body[:m.start()].count('\n')
            results.append((f.replace(ROOT+"/",""),n,bl,lock))
print(json.dumps(results,indent=0))
EOF

napi_polls = {}   # pollfn -> list of (file, line)
napi_calls = []   # (file, line, pollfn)
out = subprocess.run(["/usr/bin/rg", "-n", "--no-heading", "-g", "*.c",
                      r"netif_napi_add", "drivers", "net"],
                     cwd=ROOT, capture_output=True, text=True).stdout
for line in out.splitlines():
    m = re.match(r"([^:]+):(\d+):(.*)", line)
    if not m: continue
    f, ln, txt = m.group(1), int(m.group(2)), m.group(3)
    # netif_napi_add(dev, &napi, poll_fn, weight)
    mm = re.search(r"netif_napi_add(?:_exclusive|_weight|_irq)?\s*\(([^;]*)", txt)
    if not mm: continue
    args = mm.group(1)
    parts = [p.strip() for p in args.split(",")]
    # poll fn is typically 3rd arg
    fn = None
    for p in parts[1:4]:
        if re.match(r"^[a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*$", p) and p not in ("NAPI_POLL_WEIGHT",):
            if parts.index(p) >= 1:
                fn = p; break
    if fn:
        napi_polls.setdefault(fn, []).append((f, ln))
        napi_calls.append((f, ln, fn))

print(f"NAPI poll fns found: {len(napi_polls)}")

# Step 2: find tasklet callbacks wired via tasklet_init/tasklet_setup/DECLARE_TASKLET
tasklet_cbs = {}
out2 = subprocess.run(["/usr/bin/rg", "-n", "--no-heading", "-g", "*.c",
                       r"tasklet_init\s*\(|tasklet_setup\s*\(|DECLARE_TASKLET", "drivers", "net"],
                      cwd=ROOT, capture_output=True, text=True).stdout
for line in out2.splitlines():
    m = re.match(r"([^:]+):(\d+):(.*)", line)
    if not m: continue
    f, ln, txt = m.group(1), int(m.group(2)), m.group(3)
    mm = re.search(r"tasklet_(?:init|setup)\s*\([^,]+,\s*([a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*)", txt)
    if mm:
        tasklet_cbs.setdefault(mm.group(1), []).append((f, ln))
        continue
    mm = re.search(r"DECLARE_TASKLET(?:_DISABLED)?\s*\(\s*([a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*)\s*,\s*([a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*)", txt)
    if mm:
        tasklet_cbs.setdefault(mm.group(2), []).append((f, ln))

print(f"tasklet cbs found: {len(tasklet_cbs)}")

# Step 3: extract function bodies for all these callbacks, look for plain spin_lock
def extract_body(fname, fn):
    path = os.path.join(ROOT, fname)
    try:
        src = open(path, errors="replace").read()
    except OSError:
        return None, None
    # find definition: fn(...) {  ... may be multi-line signature
    pat = re.compile(r"^[ \t]*(?:static\s+)?(?:inline\s+)?(?:void|int|irqreturn_t|u\d+|unsigned|long|bool)\s+" + re.escape(fn) + r"\s*\(", re.M)
    m = pat.search(src)
    if not m:
        pat2 = re.compile(r"^[ \t]*" + re.escape(fn) + r"\s*\(", re.M)
        m = pat2.search(src)
        if not m:
            return None, None
    start = m.start()
    # find opening brace after signature
    bidx = src.find("{", m.end())
    if bidx == -1: return None, None
    depth = 0
    i = bidx
    while i < len(src):
        c = src[i]
        if c == "{": depth += 1
        elif c == "}":
            depth -= 1
            if depth == 0: break
        i += 1
    body = src[bidx:i+1]
    line_no = src[:start].count("\n") + 1
    return body, line_no

results = []
for kind, cmap in (("napi", napi_polls), ("tasklet", tasklet_cbs)):
    for fn, sites in cmap.items():
        for (f, ln) in sites:
            body, defline = extract_body(f, fn)
            if body is None: continue
            if "spin_lock" not in body: continue
            # find plain spin_lock( (not _bh, _irq, _irqsave, _nested...)
            plain = re.findall(r"spin_lock(?:_nested(?:_irqsave)?)?\s*\(\s*([^;]+?)\s*\)", body)
            plain = [p for p in plain if "flags" not in p.split(",")[-1:][0][:40] or True]
            bh = re.findall(r"spin_lock_bh\s*\(", body)
            irq = re.findall(r"spin_lock_irq(?:save)?\s*\(", body)
            if plain:
                results.append({
                    "kind": kind, "fn": fn, "file": f, "reg_line": ln, "def_line": defline,
                    "plain_locks": plain, "bh_sites": len(bh), "irq_sites": len(irq),
                })

print(f"callbacks with plain spin_lock in body: {len(results)}")
for r in results:
    print(f"[{r['kind']}] {r['fn']}  {r['file']}:{r['def_line']} (reg@{r['reg_line']}) plain={r['plain_locks']} bh={r['bh_sites']} irq={r['irq_sites']}")

with open(os.path.join(os.environ.get("TMPDIR","/tmp"), "i032", "scan_results.json"), "w") as fh:
    json.dump(results, fh, indent=2)

        c = src[i]
        if c == "{": depth += 1
        elif c == "}":
            depth -= 1
            if depth == 0: break
        i += 1
    body = src[bidx:i+1]
    line_no = src[:start].count("\n") + 1
    return body, line_no

results = []
for kind, cmap in (("napi", napi_polls), ("tasklet", tasklet_cbs)):
    for fn, sites in cmap.items():
        for (f, ln) in sites:
            body, defline = extract_body(f, fn)
            if body is None: continue
            if "spin_lock" not in body: continue
            # find plain spin_lock( (not _bh, _irq, _irqsave, _nested...)
            plain = re.findall(r"spin_lock(?:_nested(?:_irqsave)?)?\s*\(\s*([^;]+?)\s*\)", body)
            plain = [p for p in plain if "flags" not in p.split(",")[-1:][0][:40] or True]
            bh = re.findall(r"spin_lock_bh\s*\(", body)
            irq = re.findall(r"spin_lock_irq(?:save)?\s*\(", body)
            if plain:
                results.append({
                    "kind": kind, "fn": fn, "file": f, "reg_line": ln, "def_line": defline,
                    "plain_locks": plain, "bh_sites": len(bh), "irq_sites": len(irq),
                })

print(f"callbacks with plain spin_lock in body: {len(results)}")
for r in results:
    print(f"[{r['kind']}] {r['fn']}  {r['file']}:{r['def_line']} (reg@{r['reg_line']}) plain={r['plain_locks']} bh={r['bh_sites']} irq={r['irq_sites']}")

with open(os.path.join(os.environ.get("TMPDIR","/tmp"), "i032", "scan_results.json"), "w") as fh:
    json.dump(results, fh, indent=2)

In modern kernels, `dev_watchdog` is a `timer_list` on the netdev, so ndo_tx_timeout runs from TIMER softirq context!). Hmm. That's a timer-softirq path (branch2), but the pairing here is tasklet (NET softirq) vs timer softirq — both softirq. Deadlock between two softirqs on same CPU: a TIMER softirq holder spinning while a (HI) TASKLET softirq wants the lock — softirqs don't preempt each other on the same CPU (ksoftirqd runs them one at a time, and do_softirq processes pending bits sequentially, not nested). Actually a softirq cannot be interrupted by another softirq on the same CPU (softirq contexts don't nest except irq->softirq). So softirq-vs-softirq same-CPU can't deadlock.   "one_line_summary": "staging: ks7010: disable bh on tx_dev_lock",
  "vulnerability_summary": "tx_dev_lock is acquired with spin_lock() in process context via workqueue path, but the same lock is acquired in xmit callback running under softirq/timer context, causing a deadlock due to missing bottom-half disabling.",
  "vulnerability_pattern": "Plain spin_lock used for data shared between process context and softirq/timer callback context, violating the invariant that softirq-safe locks must disable bottom halves.",
  "patch": "commit 058cbee52ccd7be77e373d31a4f14670cfd32018
Author: Chengfeng Ye <dg573847474@gmail.com>
Date:   Tue Sep 26 16:13:23 2023 +0000

    staging: ks7010: disable bh on tx_dev_lock
    
    As &priv->tx_dev.tx_dev_lock is also acquired by xmit callback which
    could be call from timer under softirq context, use spin_lock_bh()
    on it to prevent potential deadlock.
    
    hostif_sme_work()
    --> hostif_sme_set_pmksa()
    --> hostif_mib_set_request()
    --> ks_wlan_hw_tx()
    --> spin_lock(&priv->tx_dev.tx_dev_lock)
    
    ks_wlan_start_xmit()
    --> hostif_data_request()
    --> ks_wlan_hw_tx()
    --> spin_lock(&priv->tx_dev.tx_dev_lock)
    
    Signed-off-by: Chengfeng Ye <dg573847474@gmail.com>
    Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20230926161323.41928-1-dg573847474@gmail.com
    Signed-off-by: Greg Kroah-Hartman <gregkh@linuxfoundation.org>

diff --git a/drivers/staging/ks7010/ks7010_sdio.c b/drivers/staging/ks7010/ks7010_sdio.c
index 9fb118e77a1f..f1d44e4955fc 100644
--- a/drivers/staging/ks7010/ks7010_sdio.c
+++ b/drivers/staging/ks7010/ks7010_sdio.c
@@ -395,9 +395,9 @@ int ks_wlan_hw_tx(struct ks_wlan_private *priv, void *p, unsigned long size,
 	priv->hostt.buff[priv->hostt.qtail] = le16_to_cpu(hdr->event);
 	priv->hostt.qtail = (priv->hostt.qtail + 1) % SME_EVENT_BUFF_SIZE;
 
-	spin_lock(&priv->tx_dev.tx_dev_lock);
+	spin_lock_bh(&priv->tx_dev.tx_dev_lock);
 	result = enqueue_txdev(priv, p, size, complete_handler, skb);
-	spin_unlock(&priv->tx_dev.tx_dev_lock);
+	spin_unlock_bh(&priv->tx_dev.tx_dev_lock);
 
 	if (txq_has_space(priv))
 		queue_delayed_work(priv->wq, &priv->rw_dwork, 0);
"
}

def find_body(src, name):
    pat = re.compile(r'\b' + re.escape(name) + r'\s*\([^;{]*?\)\s*\{', re.S)
    for m in pat.finditer(src):
        start = m.end(); depth = 1; i = start
        while i < len(src) and depth > 0:
            c = src[i]
            if c == '{': depth += 1
            elif c == '}': depth -= 1
            i += 1
        line = src[:m.start()].count("\n") + 1
        return src[m.start():i], line
    return None, None

# find all lines within each target file where the plain spin_lock(<lock obj>) occurs, and report enclosing function
for relf, func, lockobj in targets:
    path = os.path.join(ROOT, relf)
    with open(path, errors="replace") as fh: src = fh.read()
    lines = src.split("\n")
    # build map of line -> enclosing function by scanning for definitions
    funcs = []  # (start, end, name)
    for m in re.finditer(r'^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_ \*\t\n]*?\b([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)\s*\([^;{]*?\)\s*\{', src, re.M | re.S):

        i = m.end(); depth = 1
        while i < len(src) and depth > 0:
            c = src[i]
            if c == '{': depth += 1
            elif c == '}': depth -= 1
            i += 1
        funcs.append((start, i, m.group(1)))
    print(f"\n### {relf} lock={lockobj}")
    for i, ln in enumerate(lines):
        mm = re.search(r'spin_lock\s*\(\s*&?\s*' + re.escape(lockobj.split('.')[-1]) + r'\b', ln)
        if mm:

            owner = "?"

  "patch": "commit 058cbee52ccd7be77e373d31a4f14670cfd32018
Author: Chengfeng Ye <dg573847474@gmail.com>
Date:   Tue Sep 26 16:13:23 2023 +0000

    staging: ks7010: disable bh on tx_dev_lock
    
    As &priv->tx_dev.tx_dev_lock is also acquired by xmit callback which
    could be call from timer under softirq context, use spin_lock_bh()
    on it to prevent potential deadlock.

    --> ks_wlan_hw_tx()

Now I need a strategy. The invariant: a lock acquired inside a tasklet callback body or NAPI poll (softirq context) AND acquired with plain spin_lock() in process context (worker, ioctl, open/close, config, firmware request).

Key: both sides must take the SAME lock, one side in softirq context (tasklet/NAPI poll), other side process context with plain spin_lock (not _bh, not _irqsave... well _irqsave wouldn't prevent softirq — actually spin_lock_irqsave disables interrupts on local CPU, which also prevents softirqs on that CPU since softirqs run with interrupts enabled... Actually local IRQ disable does prevent softirq execution on that CPU. But the branch specifically says "process side uses plain spin_lock instead of spin_lock_bh". spin_lock_irqsave would also be safe against softirq on the same CPU because softirqs cannot run when irqs are disabled. So focus on plain spin_lock.

Let me write a script to analyze candidate files: for each tasklet callback function (registered via tasklet_init/tasklet_setup/DECLARE_TASKLET), extract lock names acquired inside; then search the file/project for plain spin_lock on the same lock in process context.

A practical approach: for each candidate file, get the tasklet callback function name, then find spin_lock calls within that function body, note the lock expression, then search for other plain spin_lock(&same) usages elsewhere and check the context of those (e.g., in a workqueue function, ioctl, etc.).

Let me write a Python script to do a first pass on the net-related tasklet files. Also NAPI poll functions: for each napi_schedule file, the poll function passed to netif_napi_add. That's more work; let me start with tasklets since the branch is "tasklet-napi-softirq-lock".

Note exclusions: xmit-callback paths (ndo_start_xmit) and timer callbacks are other branches. But a tasklet that is scheduled from xmit is still a tasklet callback — the branch says "Exclude xmit-callback and timer-callback paths already covered by the xmit-softirq-lock and timer-dwork-softirq-lock branches." So exclude ndo_start_xmit itself and timer_list callbacks. Tasklet bodies are in scope even if scheduled from xmit? Hmm, the intent says "tasklet_schedule/tasklet_hi_schedule callback bodies, NAPI poll functions reached via napi_schedule, or other NET_RX/NET_TX softirq callbacks" are in scope. So tasklet callback bodies are in scope. But we should avoid re-reporting what the xmit branch covers (locks shared between workqueue xmit path and ndo_start_xmit). A tasklet callback is distinct from ndo_start_xmit.

Let me write the analysis script.

Plan:
1. For each file in tasklet_net.txt, parse tasklet init: `tasklet_init(&x, func, data)`, `tasklet_setup(&x, func)`, `DECLARE_TASKLET(name, func, data)`, `tasklet_hi_...`.
2. Get the callback function name, find its definition, extract spin_lock/spin_lock_irqsave/etc. calls with lock expressions inside the body (also functions called from it — but keep it to direct body first, then extend manually).
3. For each lock expression, search whole tree for plain `spin_lock(&expr)` or `spin_lock(expr)` occurrences, and classify context.

This is complex; let me do it semi-automatically with Python and then manually triage the top candidates.

Actually, let me think about which are the most likely known bugs of this shape in older kernels (this tree has ks7010 staging, rtl8192u, etc. — looks like ~v4.x kernel, maybe 4.9-4.12 era given tasklet_init old-style and staging content). Known CVE-like bugs of this shape:
- drivers/staging/rtl8192u ieee80211_softmac: `ieee80211_...` locks? 
- wlan-ng?
- carl9170 tx.c has `carl9170_tx_process`?
- rt2x00 tasklet?
- ks8842?
- smc91x?
- The seed itself (ks7010) is in this tree — interesting: s03 includes ks7010. That's the demonstration; the fact f003 for i004 xmit-softirq-lock snapshot=s03 means the seed's tree IS s03? Wait, Fact f003: intent=i004 snapshot=s03 branch=xmit-softirq-lock. The xmit branch on s03 presumably found the ks7010 seed itself (since s03 contains ks7010 staging driver with the bug). Hmm, but seed is "staging ks7010" — and i004 searched s03 for xmit-softirq-lock... that likely found the actual seed bug present in s03. But our branch is tasklet-napi; we must not report the seed (ks7010 tx_dev_lock via xmit). Note ks7010 also uses tasklet in ks_hostif.c — but that's the same driver; must be careful: the seed must never be reported. The seed mechanism is tx_dev_lock in ks7010_sdio.c. If ks7010 has another lock with tasklet-vs-process mismatch, that could be a different finding, but risky. Let's look but be careful.

TASKLET/NAPI-softirq analogue of the seed's missing-BH-disable invariant in snapshot s02. LOCK OBJECT: struct fs_enet_private.tx_lock, taken plainly at exactly three sites in the file (97, 520, 774) with zero spin_lock_bh/local_bh_disable anywhere (grep count 0). UNTRUSTED SOURCE: attacker-influenced concurrency, not data — any inbound packet or DMA event on the shared IRQ (request_irq(fs_enet_interrupt, IRQF_SHARED) at fs_enet-main.c:741) that makes fs_enet_interrupt call napi_schedule_prep (line 340) / __napi_schedule (line 348), plus any device close (ifconfig down / netlink). SOFTIRQ SIDE: fs_enet_napi (NAPI poll fn, def line 84, registered via netif_napi_add_weight at line 1016) takes the SAME fep->tx_lock with plain spin_lock at line 97 (unlock 186) and reaps TX descriptors, frees skbs and possibly restarts TX while looping up to budget — NET_RX softirq context with BH enabled.   "patch": "commit 058cbee52ccd7be77e373d31a4f14670cfd32018

    staging: ks7010: disable bh on tx_dev_lock
    
    As &priv->tx_dev.tx_dev_lock is also acquired by xmit callback which
    could be call from timer under softirq context, use spin_lock_bh()
    on it to prevent potential deadlock.

  "one_line_summary": "staging: ks7010: disable bh on tx_dev_lock",
  "vulnerability_summary": "tx_dev_lock is acquired with spin_lock() in process context via workqueue path, but the same lock is acquired in xmit callback running under softirq/timer context, causing a deadlock due to missing bottom-half disabling.",
  "vulnerability_pattern": "Plain spin_lock used for data shared between process context and softirq/timer callback context, violating the invariant that softirq-safe locks must disable bottom halves.",
  "patch": "commit 058cbee52ccd7be77e373d31a4f14670cfd32018
Author: Chengfeng Ye <dg573847474@gmail.com>
Date:   Tue Sep 26 16:13:23 2023 +0000

    staging: ks7010: disable bh on tx_dev_lock
    
    As &priv->tx_dev.tx_dev_lock is also acquired by xmit callback which
    could be call from timer under softirq context, use spin_lock_bh()
    on it to prevent potential deadlock.
    
    hostif_sme_work()
    --> hostif_sme_set_pmksa()
    --> hostif_mib_set_request()
    --> ks_wlan_hw_tx()
    --> spin_lock(&priv->tx_dev.tx_dev_lock)
    
    ks_wlan_start_xmit()
    --> hostif_data_request()
    --> ks_wlan_hw_tx()
    --> spin_lock(&priv->tx_dev.tx_dev_lock)
    
    Signed-off-by: Chengfeng Ye <dg573847474@gmail.com>

    Signed-off-by: Greg Kroah-Hartman <gregkh@linuxfoundation.org>

content.thinking:
smc91x: line 1222 has plain `spin_lock(&lp->lock);` in what appears to be smc_hardware_send_pkt? Let me check. Line 551 is smc_hardware_send_pkt (the tasklet callback). Line 1222 is inside... let's check what function. And what locks the tasklet uses. Actually line 1222's `spin_lock(&lp->lock)` — need to see which function. But wait — the important direction: process context takes plain spin_lock; the tasklet/softirq side takes the same lock. In smc91x, most sites use spin_lock_irq, which disables IRQs and thereby also prevents softirqs on the same CPU (local IRQ disable prevents softirq processing). So a tasklet taking the lock while a process-context holds it with spin_lock_irq: tasklet runs in softirq; if process context disabled IRQs, softirq can't run on that CPU until enabled — so no deadlock. Plain spin_lock at 1222: which function?
